_transcription: COMPLETE — all five sections, 52 rows / 38 printed question numbers. The paper is bilingual on alternating pages and the alternating hypothesis HELD: idx 0 cover (Series PQ1RS/1, Set - 2, Q.P. Code 65/1/2), idx 1 Hindi instructions, and every EVEN index 2..22 is English (its odd predecessor is the Hindi of the same block). Sections A-D come from idx 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16; Section E from idx 18 (Case Study - 1 / Q36 passage), idx 20 (Q36 sub-parts + Case Study - 2 / Q37) and idx 22 (Case Study - 3 / Q38). Option labels are printed (A) (B) (C) (D), upper case, and stored upper case. Decimal points are printed as a RAISED dot (0.6 in Q29) and written as 0{\cdot}6. All 20 Section-A answers are the official marking scheme's, verbatim, from ms idx 2-6; every one of my own derivations agreed with it. THE SET IS A RESHUFFLE OF 65/1/1: 39 of these 52 rows are word-for-word the reference paper's, reshuffled AND renumbered in both directions, and their stem/context/option LaTeX is REUSED byte-for-byte after confirming each on MY page (brief section 6, recommended method) so they dedup at commit; 13 rows are genuinely new (Q2, Q6, Q13, Q15, Q18, Q24a, Q24b, Q25, Q27, Q28, Q32a, Q32b, Q34), and each of those was verified twice — once on the question page and once against its reprint in the marking scheme. THE NEAR-TRAP, and the reason content-matching is not optional: this paper's Q2 asks for the integrating factor of x dy/dx - y = x^4 - 3x with options x / -x / x^-1 / log(x^-1), while 65/1/1's Q8 is a DIFFERENT integrating-factor MCQ ((1 - x^2) dy/dx + xy = ax, options all fractions). They occupy matching slots in the reshuffle and share a topic; reusing the reference row would have shipped the wrong stem and the wrong four options. Case-study headings differ between the sets for the SAME passage — the turbulence passage is 'Case Study - 1' here and 'Case Study - 2' in 65/1/1, and the OSVD passage is 'Case Study - 3' here and 'Case Study - 1' there — so each label is recorded in _caseStudyLabel and kept OUT of context, exactly as brief section 5 requires. plan.txt listed 2 SKIPs (its Q33#1 and Q37#1); both were transcribed anyway by reusing the reference LaTeX, and its 34-item TRANSCRIBE list proved unreliable in both directions here (29 of the questions it asked for are in fact reference duplicates).

questions.context:
According to recent research, air turbulence has increased in various regions around the world due to climate change. Turbulence makes flights bumpy and often delays the flights.

Assume that, an airplane observes severe turbulence, moderate turbulence or light turbulence with equal probabilities. Further, the chance of an airplane reaching late to the destination are 55%, 37% and 17% due to severe, moderate and light turbulence respectively.

On the basis of the above information, answer the following questions :
questions.stem: Find the probability that an airplane reached its destination late.
